descriptionChirho: To breathe out words or testimony, especially used of witnesses who 'breathe out' lies or truth (Hifil figurative sense of exhaling speech).
To blow physically as wind or breath, including the breeze blowing on a garden or God blowing breath upon something (Qal and Hifil literal blowing).
To pant or gasp with eager desire or haste, used of a vision hastening toward fulfillment or of one who pants with longing.
To blow upon coals or strife so as to set aflame or inflame, a figurative extension of blowing meaning to stir up or kindle trouble.
To puff or blow contemptuously at someone, expressing disdain or dismissal of enemies or adversaries.
